messages.subject: Feature Request
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ian
I am totally loving Deducer.
I would like to put in two simple requests for improvements when you
next do some work on the program:
1. Can we have 95% CI as an option in Analysis>Descriptives, please?
2. It would *incredible* if deducer classes could be outputted to the
terminal as LaTeX tables. I have been able to take some output from
Descriptives and do:

xtable(as.data.frame(Deducer.Descriptive.Table)))

and this comes out just about OK, but these R functions can't swallow
two.sample.test or contingency.table classes and other more complex
outputs.

Adding this functionality would be an incredible boon. it should also
open up using Sweave more with deducer.

Thanks again for all your hard work.

messages.subject: Re: Feature Request
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

On Tue, Feb 1, 2011 at 12:14 PM, Ben <drbe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Ian
> I am totally loving Deducer.

I'm glad you like it.

> I would like to put in two simple requests for improvements when you
> next do some work on the program:
> 1. Can we have 95% CI as an option in Analysis>Descriptives, please?

I'll consider that for the next version. The only reason I would
hesitate is that its not really descriptive, its inferential. As of
now, there are two ways to get the interval. 1. You can enter a custom
formula into the descriptive dialog. 2. The one-sample test dialog
outputs an interval with the t-test.

> 2. It would *incredible* if deducer classes could be outputted to the
> terminal as LaTeX tables. I have been able to take some output from
> Descriptives and do:
>
> xtable(as.data.frame(Deducer.Descriptive.Table)))
>
> and this comes out just about OK, but these R functions can't swallow
> two.sample.test or contingency.table classes and other more complex
> outputs.
>
> Adding this functionality would be an incredible boon. it should also
> open up using Sweave more with deducer.

one quick solution is to override the print functions to call xtable.
Doing 4 of these will go along way:

print.data.frame <- function(x,...) print(xtable(x))
print.table <- function(x,...) print(xtable(x))
print.matrix <- function(x,...) print(xtable(x))
print.list <- function(x) lapply(x,print)

data(mtcars)
print(descriptive.table(vars = d(mpg,cyl) ,
	strata = d(hp),data= mtcars,
	func.names =c("Mean","St. Deviation","Valid N")))

print(descriptive.table(d(mpg,cyl,disp),vs,mtcars,func.names
=c("Mean","St. Deviation","Valid N")))
print(two.sample.test(formula=d(mpg,cyl,disp) ~ vs,
		data=mtcars,
		test=t.test,
		alternative="two.sided")
)

cheers,
ian

version of deducer by default. You can either install from the source,
or upgrade your R. You can use sessionInfo() to find out what version
of deducer you are using. It should be 0.4-3.

messages.subject: Re: Consistent Error with t tests
messages.body_plain:
Ben,

If you are having data related problems it is best to post the data
with it to get a reproducible error. It is much easier to see what is
going on in that case and to communicate back to you the issue. The
easiest way to do this is paste the result of dput(all)

The problem is that you have one cell of your anova with only one
observation. I can't remember what the official "rule of thumb" is
regarding cell sizes, but you should definitely have more than 5.
Consider pooling some of your groups or if nyha is ordered treating it
as continuous and using simple linear regression.

#all only has one observation with nyha==4 so the following will fail
all <- data.frame(ClimbIndex=rnorm(110),nyha=c(rep(0,18),rep(1,6),rep(2,52),rep(3,33),rep(4,1)))
k.sample.test(formula=d(ClimbIndex) ~
nyha,data=all,test=oneway.test,var.equal=TRUE)
oneway.test(ClimbIndex~factor(nyha),data=all,var.equal=TRUE)

#all2 has two observations in 4, so it will work
all2 <- data.frame(ClimbIndex=rnorm(110),nyha=c(rep(0,18),rep(1,6),rep(2,52),rep(3,32),rep(4,2)))
k.sample.test(formula=d(ClimbIndex) ~
nyha,data=all2,test=oneway.test,var.equal=TRUE)
oneway.test(ClimbIndex~factor(nyha),data=all2,var.equal=TRUE)

Best,
Ian

messages.subject: Re: Odds Ratio
messages.body_plain:
There isn't a way to do that within the GUI. The odds ratios are just
the e^coefficients. You can get confidence intervals with the confint
function. So you can do something like the following:

> model.glm <- glm(formula=vs>0.0 ~ mpg + cyl + disp,family=binomial(),data=mtcars,na.action=na.omit)
> summary(model.glm)

    data = mtcars, na.action = na.omit)

messages.subject: rJava binary reference issue
messages.body_plain:
Ruud,

It sounds like your R libraries have gotten crossed between 2.12 and
2.10. You are trying to use an rJava (a dependency of Deducer) that
was built for R 2.10. try reinstalling rJava. If that doesn't work, go
into Library > Frameworks > R.framework > Versions and delete any old
versions of R. Your crossed libraries will likely mess up more than
just deducer.

Ian
